messages:
emily_support: FYI customer ticket #7892 — they see a P99 jump ~3x starting ~03:45 UTC. Our dashboard shows a big step but the raw histogram panels look relatively flat. Can someone sanity-check whether this is a calc/rollup issue or real latency? @raj_sre ? :eyes:

alertbot: [AUTO] anomaly-detect triggered for redwood.prod.p99_requests (score: 0.82) at 2026-03-12T03:46:12Z — created incident INC-7892 :rotating_light:

raj_sre: I can look. Two quick asks: 1) which dashboard panel is the customer reading? 2) can someone paste the PromQL / query used for p99? Different functions give very different outputs (histogram_quantile vs quantile_over_time).

emily_support: Panel is "API / p99 by api_key" (dash id 4821). Support copied the metric as the standard p99 panel we ship. Here's what the dash uses (copied from panel):

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1h])) by (le, api_key))
```

emily_support: Customer says when they look at the raw histogram heatmap for the same period (5m buckets) they don't see the spike.

ben_metrics: That query uses 1h rollup buckets (rate over 1h) — our rollup service switched default aggregation window to 1h at 03:30 UTC for retention-optimized views. If you compute quantiles after you roll up (i.e., compress buckets) you can get amplification at the tail depending on sample distribution.

maria_ops: I see ingestion partitions for raw-histograms lagging around 03:40-03:50 (kafka consumer caught up at 03:59). Could be that rollups were operating on partial/late data and merged approximate sketches.

charlie_engineer: To add: we deployed a change to the aggregator at 03:27 that toggled the sketch merge algorithm from "tdigest-v1" to "tdigest-merge-opt" (smaller memory but slightly biased for small counts). If rollups ran while consumers were lagging that could make the merged sketches overestimate the 99th.

raj_sre: Ok, likely explanation: 1) consumers lag -> rollup computed from incomplete/unbalanced shards; 2) new tdigest merge made tail heavier; 3) dashboard query uses 1h rollup which amplifies the bias. That matches the timeline.

emily_support: Can someone produce quick reproducible queries I can show the customer that demonstrate the difference (raw vs rollup)?

ben_metrics: Yes — compare these two:

Raw 5m-based p99 (recommended):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, api_key))
```
Rolled-up 1h-based p99 (what dash shows):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1h])) by (le, api_key))
```
Difference should be visible around 03:45-03:55 for the affected api_key.

maria_ops: For a deeper check, run the raw histogram export for the api_key and recompute quantiles offline. Quick command we use internally: 
```
./bin/recompute-quantiles --start 2026-03-12T03:00Z --end 2026-03-12T04:00Z --api-key=acct-452 --from=raw-histograms --out=tmp/p99-recompute.json
```
This will use exact bucket counts and avoid any sketch merges.

charlie_engineer: I reproduced locally by replaying a subset of messages and running our tdigest comparator tool. With the new merge algorithm I see ~2.8x inflation at 99th for the same sample stream when shard counts < 200. Code: 
```
# run from infra/tools
go run simulate/quantile_compare.go --samples 1000 --shards 50 --merge=tdigest-merge-opt
```
Outputs: median bias: 0.02, p99 bias: 2.8x.

raj_sre: Mitigations:
- Short-term: change the dashboard panels to use 5m-based query for customer-facing views (less aggregation bias). I can push a one-line patch to dash 4821 to replace `1h` -> `5m` for the API key rows.
- Short-term alternative: add a tooltip in the dashboard explaining that rollups may bias tail metrics if consumer lag / sketch merges happened.
- Medium-term: revert tdigest-merge-opt rollout and roll back aggregator config to tdigest-v1 until we vet the bias.
- Long-term: compute p99 from raw histograms using deterministic merge at rollup time or store both rollup-sketch and exact-aggregated histogram for last 6 hours.

emily_support: For communication — propose: "We investigated and found the dashboard was using hourly rollups + a recent aggregation change. These can bias 99th percentile when data is partial/late. We will patch the dashboard to show a 5m view while we roll back the aggregation change. No customer requests were affected (no retries/timeouts recorded) — this is a metrics surface discrepancy." Thoughts?

ben_metrics: LGTM. Add ETA for rollback and dashboard patch. I'm +1 for immediate dash patch.

maria_ops: I'll open a restart/rollback ticket for the aggregator change (AGG-2345) and schedule a fast rollback window at 04:15 UTC. I'll also check whether any other rollups merged during the consumer lag window and flag affected orgs.

charlie_engineer: I'll prepare the rollback PR and a short unit test to catch p99 inflation on small shard counts. Will tag @raj_sre for quick review.

raj_sre: I'll push the dashboard patch now (5m window) and add a temporary note on the panel. Pushing change to staging first then prod asap. Patch: replace `1h` -> `5m` on panels 4821/4822.

emily_support: Thanks all. I'll send an interim message to the customer with the suggested language and ETA for the rollback + note that this appears to be a metrics calculation issue not an application outage.

ben_metrics: Postmortem checklist items:
- validate rollup window configs don't change without a canary run
- add a sanity-check that compares raw vs rolled p99 and alerts on >2x divergence
- add a consumer-lag guard that pauses rollups when lag > 5m

alertbot: [AUTO] incident INC-7892 updated: status -> investigating, owner -> maria_ops, severity -> P2

emily_support: I'll keep the thread updated with customer replies. Thanks team :pray:
